2026 SEMA Show • Mitsubishi Returns to Las Vegas With the Fresh 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition
Volkswagen Halts the Development of the ID. Golf. "We Can't Afford It!"
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Volkswagen has officially suspended preliminary development work on its highly anticipated all-electric ID Golf at its headquarters in Wolfsburg. In an internal memo sent to employees earlier today, the automaker's CEO bluntly states: "We simply can't afford this work right now!"
Thomas Schafer, CEO of Volkswagen, informed employees about the halt of the project on Friday, October 30. The unexpected decision confirms the mounting financial distress that Europe's largest auto group has been going through. The auto giant is currently going through a massive structural overhaul.
The decision to freeze the project was driven by severe cost pressures at the flagship Wolfsburg plant, which has fallen short of its cost-cutting goals by a massive 300 million euros, which translates to $335 million.
The Volkswagen Group reported a 5.9 million euro ($6.6 million) operating loss for the third quarter. This marks Volkswagen's largest quarterly deficit in over a decade. The previous massive deficit dated way back to the 2015 Dieselgate emissions scandal.
Photo: Volkswagen The Volkswagen ID Golf , if it ever hits the market, is set to be underpinned by Volkswagen’s Scalable Systems Platform (SSP), designed to merge the existing architecture into a unified, highly efficient platform that would significantly lower production costs and help the group's models compete with low-cost Chinese rivals.
However, the SSP architecture has faced multiple software hurdles and development delays, heavily complicating the ID Golf's timeline. The company’s works council insists this temporary spending freeze will not push back the model’s eventual market launch, but is well aware that the freeze is yet another sign of how strained the group’s financial situation actually is.
" We simply can't afford it, " CEO Schafer told employees in the memo sent this morning, as reported by Automotive News. The halt comes amid a deeply hostile business environment. Volkswagen Group is currently moving forward with plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs and potentially close up to four factories across Germany.
While factories in Emden and Zwickau are reportedly making progress to slash jobs, they are among the sites facing potential closure. Wolfsburg itself is safe from closure, but must drastically lean out its operations.
Photo: Volkswagen Tensions are inching closer to the boiling point with the powerful union IG Metall, which has been warning of widespread strikes starting December 1, 2026, if the employer and employees do not reach a resolution.
In the meantime, Volkswagen Group's premium brand, Audi, will be investing $4 billion into a new plant in the United States. Donald Trump officially announced the Georgia assembly plant at a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia. Audi CEO Gernot Doellner even joined him on stage, leading to massive backlash steered him and the company.
As the Golf EV goes on ice, Volkswagen is leaning heavily back on internal combustion engines to preserve cash flow. VW has temporarily halted or paused production of the ID. 4 and ID. Buzz for the U.S. market. In the meantime, the production of the gas-powered eighth-generation Golf is scheduled to relocate from Wolfsburg to Puebla, Mexico, in 2027.

He Bought a Mercedes-Maybach for $227,550, Drove 200 Miles, Sold for $195,000
23 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
Depreciation is a killer, and luxury car owners know it best. Ask the owner of this 2026 Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series convertible. He bought the car back in August240. Two months and 240 miles later, he already listed it for sale.
Cars start losing value the moment they drive off the showroom floor. For ultra-luxury vehicles, depreciation is far worse, and the owner of this convertible learned it the hard way. He only kept the car for two months before he decided to get rid of it for undisclosed reasons.
He didn’t even make it too far before he listed it for sale: just 240 miles (386 kilometers). Finished in the show-stopping Manufaktur Garnet Red over a Manufaktur Crystal White interior, the SL 680 Monogram Series rides on the standard 21-inch Maybach forged wheels. It looks like the perfect spec.
The seller says he googled the number of the Maybach logos and found they should be 835, with most of them sitting on the power-operated soft top that shelters the Nappa leather upholstery that wraps the power-adjustable heated and ventilated multi-contour seats.
Photo: Cars and Bids Those seats keep the occupants secured in place during the plush ride provided by the Active Ride Control suspension, while the Airscarf neck-warming system brings a comfortable ambiance with the top down even when it’s cold outside. A Burmester High-End 3D surround system provides the soundtrack on board when the driver has had enough of the V8 orchestra.
Speaking of which, the 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged M177 V8 pushes out 577 horsepower (585 metric horsepower) and 590 pound-feet (800 Newton meters) of torque. That is what makes the ultra-luxury convertible rocket from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in just 4.0 seconds and max out at 161 mph (260 kph).
A nine-speed Speedshift MCT automatic transmission euqips the Mercedes-Maybach convertible , putting the power down through all four corners with the help of Mercedes' Performance 4MATIC+ all-wheel drive system.
The original owner of this boulevard cruiser paid $227,550 to drive it home back in August. This late October, however, he decided he no longer needed it, so he listed it for sale on Cars and Bids. The bidding stopped at $182,500, which meant a financial blow of $45,050.
Photo: Cars and Bids However, those managing the auction went on a damage-limitation mission and contacted the author of the most generous offer. The 2026 Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series ended up selling for $195,000.
The buyer got a very low-mileage luxury grand tourer with a clean Carfax, showing no accidents or mileage discrepancies. No surprise there! He also got two keys, the owner’s manuals, and the window sticker, along with the brand-new, highly discounted Maybach, while skipping the waiting list. Nothing to complain about, right?

Lavvu XL Is a Pod-Like Mobile House Designed to Impress, Yet Fully Functional
34 photos
Photo: Lavvu
Mobile living can be what you want it to be – and whatever that is, you're likely to find the right manufacturer, with the right product for you. Assuming money is not an issue, that product can be as spectacular as the prefab called Lavvu XL.
Lavvu XL is the flagship product from Italian startup Lavvu. It's also the biggest module they have on offer or, better said, that they plan to offer – a unit that stands out for its construction, its functionality, and its eye-catching design.
We're talking about a mobile home, though mobility is largely limited. Being a prefab, this unit can be shipped to your desired location fully assembled and furnished, on the back of flatbed truck or a large trailer, and set up quickly and with little hassle. Of course, all the hassle about land prep and utilities has to take place beforehand, but that's another story.
In the large segment of mobile homes , the Lavvu XL sits in the prefab niche. It's mobile in the sense that you could pack it up and move it to another location if you had to, but it's obviously designed to stay put wherever it's delivered for longer stretches, if not permanently.
Photo: Lavvu Being a prefabricated module means installation is also easier than with a typical house, in that you won't require pouring a foundation or waiting for years until it's livable. It's a "to-go" home, but of the nicest kind.
The Lavvu XL is the fourth and largest model from Lavvu, offering 22 square meters (237 square feet) of living space. It comes in at 9.7 meters (32 feet) of total length and it's almost entirely wrapped in glass, with floor-to-ceiling opening windows offering an almost unmatched sense of openness and outdoor living.
Where it's not made of glass, it's made of steel. The XL has a steel frame and construction, with a precision-cut steel plate frame and interior partitions made of light-gauge steel framing and lightweight insulation panels. It weighs under 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs), though weight is only an issue when you have it transported to the location.
Photo: Lavvu The XL is available in two layouts, though only one in shown in renders and footage of the only completed unit so far. That would be The Retreat layout, which is imagined as a couple's floorplan with a kitchen with a dining island, a bedroom, a lounge, a full bathroom with a soaking tub, and a full wardrobe.
The Family layout retains the core features , down to the tub in the bathroom, but squeezes in three sleeping areas. Since the manufacturer doesn't offer as much as a single render for it, where these three sleeping spaces would go is anyone's guess.
As you can see in the photos in the gallery and the brief video tour below, the layout is linear, much like in a container home, which means you have no proper bedroom. Instead, you have open-space living, with the only "room" inside being the bathroom, which has walls and a door for the obvious reasons.
Photo: Lavvu Yet Lavvu does its best to work around that, having the bed face the curved window at the front of the house and framing the kitchen space with help from the island. This island has a mobile counter, so you have legspace underneath when you dine and a nice work surface when you use it standing.
Though a house of glass (with some steel), the Lavvu XL doesn't lack everyday functionality . The kitchen is fully equipped, including a small fridge, a dishwasher, and a two-burner induction cooktop. You have ample storage wherever possible, from large drawers under the bed to lots of cabinets in the kitchen. There's also the oversize wardrobe at the rear of the house, taking up half of the width of the home.
The other half is taken up by the bathroom, a true spa-like space inside such a compact footprint. As much as people will romanticize the advantages of downsizing and decluttering, the reality is often that people still want home-like comforts and still need space for their stuff. This home has them both.
Photo: Lavvu Highlights in the bathroom include a handheld shower and a rain showerhead, a floating toilet, a nice sink with vanity, and dedicated space for a top-loading washing machine and a laundry basket. It's the little things that make a difference, and Lavvu clearly knows it.
This home is designed for year-round living and is meant to be hooked up to the mains for water, electricity, and waste. It comes with "smart low-consumption custom HVAC" with underfloor heating and an AC, triple-glazed windows, and high-performance insulation.
Offered fully furnished, presumably in the manner you see in the demo unit below, it's being marketed as a "sophisticated design for families and those who simply refuse to give anything up." If you "simply" refuse to give stuff up, you must be ready to pay extra.
Photo: Lavvu The Lavvu starts at €75,000 (approximately $84,000 at the current exchange rate) before tax and not taking into account extra expenses you will incur, like shipping, land prep, and utilities. This is a (half) mobile home designed for the discerning, and it will come at a price to match. View this post on Instagram A post shared by LAVVU. Live it up. (@lavvu_homes)
